Kinailangan na pansamantalang ihinto ang operasyon ng Abucay pumping station  sa Tondo, Manila dahil sa basura na nakapulupot sa impeller nito.

Pinagtulungang munang alisin ng miyembro ng MMDA Flood Control and Sewerage Management Office ang basura na tila plastic na pumasok at sumabit sa makina.

Panawagan ng MMDA: maging responsable sa pagtatapon ng basura, lalo na  plastic waste, na nagiging sanhi ng pagbara at pagkasira ng pasilidad na humihigop sa baha sa Metro Manila kapag malakas ang ulan. 
#mmda

Sa pangunguna ng Metro Manila Traffic Enforcement Districts, makipagtulungan upang maging passable at obstruction-free ang bangketa, Mabuhay Lanes, at mga pangunahing kalsada sa Kalakhang Maynila.

data.text:
Unified for National Progress: 
How Speaker Romualdez and the 19th Congress Anchor the Marcos Jr. Administration’s Stability

In a political environment often beset by partisanship and gridlock, the 19th Congress of the Philippines, under the steady leadership of Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez, stands out for its legislative cohesion, policy alignment with Malacañang, and unambiguous commitment to national progress.

From July 2022 to June 2025, the House of Representatives posted record productivity: 11,557 bills filed, 2,393 resolutions submitted, and 1,565 measures approved, of which 287 became national or local laws. Over just 188 session days, that equates to nearly 29 legislative actions per day, a pace that defies historical precedent and signals a legislature moving with purpose.

This legislative momentum is Speaker Romualdez’s capacity to harmonize the House’s priorities with those of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The 19th Congress passed 63 of the 64 measures in the Common Legislative Agenda, 33 of which were signed into law, and cleared 27 of the 28 priority bills identified by the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council (LEDAC). This extraordinary policy throughout reflects more than efficiency—it reflects strategic unity between Congress and Malacañang, a synchrony essential to stable and sustainable governance.

Romualdez’s leadership has not only supported but also operationalized the “BAGONG PILIPINAS” vision by anchoring legislative pillars to the administration’s flagship policy themes. On national sovereignty and security, landmark laws such as the Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act, Maritime Zones Act, and the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Act were passed to reinforce the Philippines’ geopolitical footing. On economic revitalization, the Maharlika Investment Fund, CREATE MORE Act, Ease of Paying Taxes law, Digital Services VAT, and natural gas and EPIRA reforms collectively modernize fiscal policy & attract critical capital for growth.

Equally important, Romualdez steered the House toward inclusive reforms in education, healthcare, & agriculture sectors that underpin long-term development. Legislation such as the ARAL Program, Expanded Tertiary Education Equivalency and Accreditation Program (ETEEAP), Electronic & Broadcast EdTech (EBET), & the Student Loan Moratorium address learning gaps; the Specialty Centers Act & Caregivers' Welfare Act expand public health access; & anti-agricultural smuggling laws and rice competitiveness reforms boost food security.

In the global sphere, the Speaker positioned the Philippines as an emerging innovation hub. At the World Summit on the Information Society in Geneva, Romualdez showcased progress under the National Innovation Agenda, including the Digital Workforce Act and initiatives to commercialize intellectual property. The payoff: the country’s Global Innovation Index ranking rose from 59th to 56th, with the Philippines recognized as among the fastest “innovation catch-ups” in the world.

What sets the 19th Congress apart is not just its legislative output but its institutional synchrony. The relationship between the House and Malacañang is marked by an uncommon alignment of vision, execution, & tempo. Romualdez has marshaled a 307-member supermajority into a cohesive body capable of translating presidential policy into actionable law without undue delay.

In an era where public trust hinges on delivery, not rhetoric, the 19th Congress under Speaker Romualdez exemplifies how disciplined leadership & coordinated governance can produce real, measurable progress. This alignment between the legislative & executive branches has not only ensured policy continuity, it has also secured the political stability that every serious development agenda requires. As the nation prepares to transition into the 20th Congress, sustaining this momentum will be critical to institutionalizing reforms, accelerating economic recovery, & protecting long-term national interests.
